record.field: Deadline timing: GST/HST return and payment (monthly filer)

Return and net tax due one month after the end of the reporting period. Excise Tax Act ss. 238(1)(b) and 228(2)(b). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/E-15/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/publications/rc4022/general-information-gst-hst-registrants.html
Deadline timing: GST/HST return and payment (quarterly filer)

Return and net tax due one month after the end of the reporting period. Excise Tax Act ss. 238(1)(b) and 228(2)(b). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/E-15/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/publications/rc4022/general-information-gst-hst-registrants.html
Deadline timing: GST/HST return and payment (annual filer)

Annual filer other than an individual: return and net tax due three months after the end of the fiscal year. Excise Tax Act ss. 238(1)(a)(iii) and 228(2)(b). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/E-15/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/publications/rc4022/general-information-gst-hst-registrants.html
Deadline timing: GST/HST quarterly instalment (annual filer)

Annual filer whose net tax reaches the instalment threshold: instalment due one month after the end of each fiscal quarter. Excise Tax Act s. 237. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/E-15/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/pay-instalment/when-to-pay.html
Deadline timing: QST return and payment (monthly filer)
Return and net tax due one month after the end of the reporting period. Act respecting the Quebec sales tax, s. 468. https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/T-0.1
Deadline timing: QST return and payment (quarterly filer)
Return and net tax due one month after the end of the reporting period. Act respecting the Quebec sales tax, s. 468. https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/T-0.1
Deadline timing: QST return and payment (annual filer)

Annual filer other than an individual: return and net tax due three months after the end of the fiscal year. Act respecting the Quebec sales tax, s. 468. https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/T-0.1
Deadline timing: QST quarterly instalment (annual filer)

Annual filer whose net tax reaches the instalment threshold: instalment due within one month after the end of each fiscal quarter. Act respecting the Quebec sales tax, s. 458.0.1. https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/T-0.1 https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/consumption-taxes/gsthst-and-qst/reporting-gst-and-qst/remittance-or-refund/gst-and-qst-instalments/
Deadline timing: Federal corporate income tax instalment (monthly)

Instalment due on the last day of each month of the taxation year. Income Tax Act s. 157(1)(a). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/ https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/resources-for-small-and-medium-businesses/2026-tax-deadlines-canadian-businesses-self-employed-individuals.html
Deadline timing: Federal corporate income tax instalment (quarterly, small CCPC)

Small Canadian-controlled private corporation: instalment due on the last day of each quarter of the taxation year. Income Tax Act s. 157(1.1). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/ https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/resources-for-small-and-medium-businesses/2026-tax-deadlines-canadian-businesses-self-employed-individuals.html
Deadline timing: Quebec corporate income tax instalment (monthly)
Instalment due on or before the last day of each month of the taxation year. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 1027(a)(i). https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Deadline timing: Quebec corporate income tax instalment (quarterly, qualified CCPC)

Qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation: instalment due on or before the last day of each three-month period of the taxation year. Taxation Act (Quebec) ss. 1027(a)(iii) and 1027.0.1. https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Deadline timing: Federal corporate income tax balance

Balance-due day of a corporation: end of the second month after the end of the taxation year. Income Tax Act ss. 157(1)(b) and 248(1) balance-due day. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/ https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/resources-for-small-and-medium-businesses/2026-tax-deadlines-canadian-businesses-self-employed-individuals.html
Deadline timing: Federal corporate income tax balance (CCPC)

Balance-due day of a CCPC that claims the small business deduction and whose taxable income of the previous year does not exceed its business limit: end of the third month after the end of the taxation year. Income Tax Act s. 248(1) balance-due day (d)(i). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/ https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/resources-for-small-and-medium-businesses/2026-tax-deadlines-canadian-businesses-self-employed-individuals.html
Deadline timing: Quebec corporate income tax balance

Balance-due day of a corporation: last day of the two-month period ending after the end of the taxation year, CCPC included. Taxation Act (Quebec) ss. 1 balance-due day and 1027(b). https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Deadline timing: T2 corporation income tax return

Return due within six months after the end of the taxation year. Income Tax Act s. 150(1)(a). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/ https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/resources-for-small-and-medium-businesses/2026-tax-deadlines-canadian-businesses-self-employed-individuals.html
Deadline timing: CO-17 corporation income tax return
Return due within six months from the end of the taxation year. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 1000(2)(a). https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/I-3
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to the CRA (quarterly)

Quarterly remitter: due on the 15th day of the month after each calendar quarter. Income Tax Regulations s. 108(1.12). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/payroll/remitting-source-deductions/how-when-remit-due-dates.html
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to the CRA (regular)

Regular remitter: due on the 15th day of the month after the month the remuneration is paid. Income Tax Regulations s. 108(1). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/payroll/remitting-source-deductions/how-when-remit-due-dates.html
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to the CRA (accelerated threshold 1)

Accelerated threshold 1: remuneration paid from the 1st to the 15th is due on the 25th of the month, from the 16th to the end of the month on the 10th of the next month. Income Tax Regulations s. 108(1.1)(a). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/payroll/remitting-source-deductions/how-when-remit-due-dates.html
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to the CRA (accelerated threshold 2)

Accelerated threshold 2: due the 3rd working day after the 7th, the 14th, the 21st and the last day of the month. Income Tax Regulations s. 108(1.1)(b). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/payroll/remitting-source-deductions/how-when-remit-due-dates.html
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to Revenu Quebec (annual)

Annual remitter (source deductions and employer contributions of the previous year of $2,400 or less): due on the 15th day of the month after the last month of the year, January 15 in most cases. Guide for employers TP-1015.G, Table 7. A day the offices of Revenu Quebec are closed is not a business day, as the guide states. https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/remitting-source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/frequency-of-remittances/
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to Revenu Quebec (quarterly)

Quarterly remitter: due on the 15th day of the month after each calendar quarter. Guide for employers TP-1015.G. A day the offices of Revenu Quebec are closed is not a business day, as the guide states. https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/remitting-source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/frequency-of-remittances/
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to Revenu Quebec (monthly)

Monthly remitter: due on the 15th day of the month after the month the remuneration is paid. Guide for employers TP-1015.G. A day the offices of Revenu Quebec are closed is not a business day, as the guide states. https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/remitting-source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/frequency-of-remittances/
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to Revenu Quebec (twice a month)

Twice-monthly remitter: remuneration paid from the 1st to the 15th is due on the 25th, from the 16th to the end of the month on the 10th of the next month. Guide for employers TP-1015.G. A day the offices of Revenu Quebec are closed is not a business day, as the guide states. https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/remitting-source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/frequency-of-remittances/
Deadline timing: Source deductions remittance to Revenu Quebec (weekly)

Weekly remitter: due the 3rd business day after the 7th, the 14th, the 21st and the last day of the month. Guide for employers TP-1015.G. A day the offices of Revenu Quebec are closed is not a business day, as the guide states. https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/remitting-source-deductions-and-employer-contributions/frequency-of-remittances/
Deadline timing: T4 slips and T4 Summary

T4 information return due on or before the last day of February of the following calendar year. Income Tax Regulations ss. 200(1) and 205(1). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/ https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/resources-for-small-and-medium-businesses/2026-tax-deadlines-canadian-businesses-self-employed-individuals.html
Deadline timing: T5 slips and T5 Summary

T5 information return (dividends, interest) due on or before the last day of February of the following calendar year. Income Tax Regulations ss. 201(1) and 205(1). https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/C.R.C.,_c._945/
Deadline timing: RL-1 slips and RL-1 Summary

RL slips and RL-1 summary due by the last day of February of the following year, together with the labour standards (CNT) contribution, the WSDRF (FDRCMO) contribution if any, and the part of the Health Services Fund balance caused by the gap between the actual and the estimated rate. The balance of Quebec income tax withheld and of QPP and QPIP contributions (summary line 48) is due with the last December remittance, not with the summary; paid with the summary, it bears interest and may bring a penalty. TP-1015.G, ss. 11.3 and 11.6. https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/rl-slips-and-summaries/sending-rl-slips-and-summaries/filing-deadline/
Deadline timing: Health Services Fund contribution reconciliation (RL-1 Summary)

The employer contribution to the Health Services Fund of the year is reconciled on the RL-1 summary, due by the last day of February of the following year. Only the part of the balance caused by the gap between the actual and the estimated contribution rate is payable by that date; the rest of the HSF balance is due with the last December remittance. TP-1015.G, ss. 6.6 and 11.6. https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/rl-slips-and-summaries/sending-rl-slips-and-summaries/filing-deadline/
Deadline timing: RL-3 slips and RL-3 Summary

RL-3 slips (investment income) and summary due by the last day of February of the following year. https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/rl-slips-and-summaries/sending-rl-slips-and-summaries/filing-deadline/
Deadline timing: CNESST statement of wages

Statement of the gross wages of the previous year, to be sent before March 15: the last day is March 14. An employer whose last worker leaves sends it at the latest 45 days after that departure. Act respecting industrial accidents and occupational diseases, s. 291, and its regulation on the statement of wages. No weekend postponement is applied: the CNESST publishes none. https://www.cnesst.gouv.qc.ca/fr/demarches-formulaires/employeurs/assurance-sante-securite-travail/obligations-annuelles-prime-assurance/declaration-salaires/production-transmission https://www.cnesst.gouv.qc.ca/fr/demarches-formulaires/employeurs/assurance-sante-securite-travail/obligations-annuelles-prime-assurance/declaration-salaires/declaration-salaires-en-retard
Deadline timing: Annual updating declaration (filed with the CO-17)

Legal person whose annual updating declaration is combined with its income tax return: due no later than six months after the end of its fiscal year. Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. https://www.quebec.ca/entreprises-et-travailleurs-autonomes/mettre-a-jour-informations/declaration-mise-a-jour/annuelle
Deadline timing: Annual registration fee (filed with the CO-17)

Legal person whose annual updating declaration is combined with its income tax return: annual registration fee payable no later than two months after the end of its fiscal year. https://www.quebec.ca/entreprises-et-travailleurs-autonomes/mettre-a-jour-informations/declaration-mise-a-jour/annuelle
Deadline timing: Annual updating declaration (May 15 to November 15)

Legal person whose declaration is not combined with its income tax return: filing period from May 15 to November 15 of each year. https://www.quebec.ca/entreprises-et-travailleurs-autonomes/mettre-a-jour-informations/declaration-mise-a-jour/annuelle

Annual filers pay quarterly instalments when their instalment base, the lesser of the net tax of the current and of the previous fiscal year, is this amount or more. Excise Tax Act s. 237(3): an instalment base under this amount is deemed nil. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/E-15/ https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/gst-hst-businesses/pay-instalment/when-to-pay.html

Annual filers pay quarterly instalments when their instalment base, the lesser of the net tax of the current and of the previous fiscal year, is this amount or more. Act respecting the Quebec sales tax, s. 458.0.3: an instalment base under this amount is deemed nil. https://www.legisquebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/document/cs/T-0.1 https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/consumption-taxes/gsthst-and-qst/reporting-gst-and-qst/remittance-or-refund/gst-and-qst-instalments/
